description: Match identifier used by Cricsheet. Usually the Cricinfo match id but not guaranteed to be. Joins to match_info and match_players.
Season of the match, such as 2018 or 2011/12.
First day of the match. Multi-day matches show only the first day here; match_info has every day.
Ground where the match was played, such as Old Trafford. Blank if not recorded.
Innings number of the delivery. Super overs continue the count (3 and up in a limited-overs match).
Over and ball in cricket notation: 23.5 is the 5th ball of the 24th over. Stored as a number, so the 10th delivery of an over (35.10) reads as 35.1. Use over_no and delivery_in_over instead.
Team batting on this delivery.
Team bowling on this delivery.
Batter who faced the delivery.
Batter at the bowler's end.
Bowler of the delivery.
Runs scored by the batter off this ball. 0 if none.
Total extras conceded on this ball. 0 if none.
Wides conceded on this ball. Blank if none.
No-balls conceded on this ball. Blank if none.
Byes conceded on this ball. Blank if none.
Leg-byes conceded on this ball. Blank if none.
Penalty runs conceded on this ball. Blank if none.

How a batter was out on this ball: bowled, caught, caught and bowled, lbw, stumped, run out, retired hurt, hit wicket, obstructing the field, hit the ball twice, handled the ball or timed out. Blank if no wicket.
Batter dismissed on this ball. Blank if no wicket.
Type of a second dismissal on the same ball, for example a retirement hurt alongside a wicket. Blank otherwise.
Batter dismissed in a second dismissal on the same ball. Blank otherwise.
Format of the match: T20 (international), ODI, TEST or IPL. Copied from match_info so you can filter deliveries without a join.
Over number taken from the ball text (35 in 35.10). An exact integer.
Delivery number within the over taken from the ball text (10 in 35.10). It counts wides and no-balls, so it can run past 6. For the legal-ball count use actual_delivery.
Legal-ball count within the over. A delivery after a wide or no-ball repeats the previous number.
True when a 4 or 6 was scored without reaching the boundary, for example all run or overthrows. Blank otherwise.
First fielder involved in a dismissal, such as the catcher. Blank if not known or no dismissal.
Second fielder involved in a dismissal. Filled only for some run outs.
Third fielder involved in a run out. Rarely filled.
male or female. Copied from match_info.
international or club (the IPL is club). Copied from match_info.
Match identifier used by Cricsheet. One row per match. Joins to ball_by_ball and match_players.
Format of the match: T20 (international), ODI, TEST or IPL.
First team listed in the Cricsheet file. The order is as filed and does not mean home or batting first.
Second team listed in the Cricsheet file.

Our classification of team1 from ICC membership lists: Full Member, Associate-ODI (an associate with ODI status for that gender) or Associate. Blank for club sides such as IPL franchises. Not part of Cricsheet.
Same as team1_icc_type for team2.
male or female.
Season of the match, such as 2018 or 2011/12.
First day of the match.
Ground where the match was played.
City of the venue, such as Dubai. Blank if not recorded.
Competition or series the match was part of, if any.
Match number within the event, if any.
Team that won the toss.
Choice made by the toss winner: bat or field.
Winning team. Blank for a draw, a no result or a tie (see outcome). A tie settled by a super over or bowl-out also leaves it blank; the side that won is in eliminator or bowl_out.
Winning margin in runs, when the match was won by runs or by an innings and runs.
Winning margin in wickets, when the match was won by wickets.
Player of the match. When the award was shared the second name is in player_of_match2.
First on-field umpire listed.
Second on-field umpire listed.
TV umpire, if recorded.
Reserve umpire, if recorded.
Match referee, if recorded.
Result when no team won: draw, no result or tie. Blank when there is a winner.
How a curtailed or unusual result was decided, such as D/L (Duckworth-Lewis, possibly Stern) or Awarded. Blank for a normal result.
Winner of an eliminator super over used to settle a tie.
Winner of a bowl-out used to settle a tied T20.
1 when the match was won by an innings (winner_runs then holds the extra runs).
Innings numbers that were super overs, comma-separated (for example 3,4). Blank if none.
Innings numbers that were declared, comma-separated (for example 1,3). Blank if none.
Scheduled overs per innings for the format, such as 20 or 50.
Overs available for the chase when a target was set, in cricket notation (40.2 is 40 overs and 2 balls). Do not sum or average it.
Runs needed when a target was set (for example after a rain revision).
Running number of this match within its type, for example the 2404th Test.
international or club (the IPL is club).
Balls expected per over, normally 6.
true when the toss was not contested and was awarded to one side. Mostly County Championship 2016 to 2019, so rare here.
Second player of the match when the award was shared.
Third umpire listed, usually a substitution during the match.
Fourth umpire listed.
Second TV umpire listed.
Second reserve umpire listed.
Last day of the match. Rest days mean end_date minus start_date is not the number of playing days; count match_dates for that.
Every playing day of the match, comma-separated, as filed by Cricsheet.
Match identifier. Joins to ball_by_ball and match_info.
Name of the person as filed for that match.
Cricsheet register id of the person. Follow a player across matches with this id, since two people can share a name. Joins to people.
Team the person played for. Blank for officials.
player, umpire, tv_umpire, reserve_umpire or match_referee. Comma-separated when one person held two roles. Blank when Cricsheet names the person without a role, mostly substitute fielders.
Cricsheet register id. One row per person. Joins to match_players.
Name as used in the Cricsheet data. Not unique: two people can share a name.
A version of the name that is unique across the register.
Id of the person on the BCCI site.
Second BCCI id where one exists.
Id on the Big Bash League site.
Id on Cricbuzz.
Id on CricHeroes.
Id on CricHQ.
Id on ESPNcricinfo.
Second ESPNcricinfo id where one exists.
Third ESPNcricinfo id where one exists.
Id on Cricingif.
Id on CricketArchive.
Second CricketArchive id where one exists.
Id on Cricket World.
Id on NV Play.
Second NV Play id where one exists.
Id on Opta.
Second Opta id where one exists.
Id on Pulse.
Second Pulse id where one exists.
